founded.what: The year a former cooper founded the house at Tours-sur-Marne, the date the house and the library both give.

place: Tours-sur-Marne, Vallée de la Marne, Champagne

kind.means: A négociant manipulant, a house in the trade's own word: it buys grapes from growers beyond its own vines and makes the wine itself at Tours-sur-Marne.

story: The house began at Tours-sur-Marne in 1812, founded by a former cooper. Its cellar master took it over in the 1880s, and when he was killed in a cellar accident in 1887 his widow ran it and joined her own name to his: Veuve Laurent-Perrier. Late in the nineteenth century she sold a Champagne with no added sugar, the Grand Vin Sans Sucre, by the house's account. Her daughter ran it after her death in 1925, and in 1939 the house was sold to a woman born into the Lanson family, whose son Bernard de Nonancourt (1920 to 2010) fought in the Resistance and in 1945 was among the soldiers who opened the wine cellar at Hitler's Eagle's Nest. He became head of the house in 1948 and led it for more than fifty years. Under him came Grand Siècle, released in 1959 as a blend of three vintages; the Cuvée Rosé, made by maceration, in 1968; and Ultra Brut, with no dosage, in 1981. Salon and Delamotte, at Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, joined the group at the end of the 1980s. In 2019 the house first printed the Itération number on a bottle of Grand Siècle.

style.line: Freshness and elegance led by Chardonnay, with no oak anywhere in the range, as the library teaches; the house names three signatures: blending reserve wines, rosé made by maceration, and Champagne with no dosage.
style.grapes: Chardonnay leads the range, with Pinot Noir and, in La Cuvée, Meunier; Grand Siècle is Chardonnay and Pinot Noir from Grand Cru villages alone.
style.reserve: Blending reserve wines is one of the house's three signatures, by its own pages; Grand Siècle is three vintages kept as reserve wines and blended together.
style.vessels: Stainless steel: the library's record of the house says no oak anywhere in the range.
style.lees: About ten years for Grand Siècle Itération 26, by the house; Les Réserves, Itération 20, rested 21 years in magnum before disgorging.
style.dosage: 7 grams a litre for Grand Siècle Itérations 23 and 25, by the house's magazine; none at all in Ultra Brut.

nv.name: La Cuvée
nv.note: The non vintage Brut, led by Chardonnay with Pinot Noir and Meunier; the Cuvée Rosé, Pinot Noir macerated on its skins since 1968, is the other bottle guests know.

cuvee.name: Grand Siècle

first.what: The year of the first release by most accounts, a blend of the 1952, 1953 and 1955 vintages; Decanter and Wikipedia date the launch 1960.

cuvee.rhythm: Each release is an Itération, numbered on the bottle since 2019, when Itérations 24 and 22, the latter in magnum, first carried it: Itération 25 blends 2008, 2007 and 2006, and Itération 26 blends 2012, 2008 and 2007.
cuvee.blend: Chardonnay leads, a little under three fifths in Itération 26 by the house, with Pinot Noir for the rest; no Meunier.
cuvee.sites: Grand Cru villages alone, eight for Itération 26 by the house: Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, Oger, Cramant and Avize in the Côte des Blancs for the Chardonnay; Tours-sur-Marne, Ambonnay, Bouzy and Verzy for the Pinot Noir.
cuvee.making: Three vintages the house judges complementary are kept as reserve wines and blended to recreate, in its words, the perfect year: 65, 25 and 10 parts of the three for Itération 26, the youngest leading. Made without oak, as the library says of the whole range, it rests about ten years on its lees before disgorging, with a dosage of 7 grams a litre.
cuvee.lees: About ten years for Itération 26, by the house's own guide to prestige cuvées.
cuvee.young: Brioche and lime zest over crisp apple, with a touch of mango, a fine, lively mousse and a creamy body that ends on a gentle, mouthwatering bitterness, by Falstaff and Gault and Millau.
cuvee.aged: Les Réserves shows the wine kept far longer, more than twenty years on its lees in magnum; no note of an older bottle was sourced, so the record names none.

forms.name: Grand Siècle Les Réserves
forms.note: Late disgorged and in magnum alone: Itération 20, of 1999, 1997 and 1996, rested 21 years under natural cork, the second such release after Itération 17.

cuvee.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, never ice cold; no need to decant; a tulip or a white wine glass.

table.house45: Laurent-Perrier is a house of Tours-sur-Marne, on the Marne, founded in 1812. Its name joins a cellar master and his widow, who ran it after his death in 1887. In 1939 it was bought by the mother of Bernard de Nonancourt, who led it for more than fifty years after the war. He gave it its signatures: a pink Champagne made by soaking Pinot Noir on its skins, a revived Champagne with no added sugar, and the prestige cuvée Grand Siècle. The style is fresh and led by Chardonnay, with no oak at all. La Cuvée is the bottle most guests know.
table.house10: Laurent-Perrier is the Tours-sur-Marne house of 1812: Chardonnay led, made without oak, and the maker of Grand Siècle.
table.cuvee45: Grand Siècle is the prestige cuvée of Laurent-Perrier, first released in 1959. Instead of one great year, it blends three vintages the house judges complementary, to recreate the perfect year. It is Chardonnay led with Pinot Noir, all from Grand Cru villages such as Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, Avize and Bouzy. Each release is an Itération, and the number is printed on the bottle. Expect brioche, lime zest and crisp apple, with a creamy body. It rests about ten years in the cellar, and I pour it at about nine degrees in a white wine glass.
table.sale: If you would like a prestige Champagne built from three vintages rather than one, Grand Siècle is Laurent-Perrier's answer, Chardonnay led and all Grand Cru. May I bring a bottle for the table?
table.cuvee10: Grand Siècle is Laurent-Perrier's prestige cuvée: three vintages blended on purpose, Chardonnay led, all from Grand Cru villages.
table.cuvee20: Grand Siècle is the prestige cuvée of Laurent-Perrier, blended from three vintages to recreate the perfect year. Each release is a numbered Itération, Chardonnay led with Pinot Noir from Grand Cru villages, aged about ten years.

guests.q: Why does Grand Siècle have no vintage on the label?
guests.a: Because it is three vintages on purpose: the house blends three years it judges complementary, such as 2012, 2008 and 2007 for Itération 26, and numbers each release instead.
The release's place in the line of Grand Siècle blends since 1959; the house began printing it on the bottle in 2019, with Itération 24.
Yes: Salon and Delamotte, both of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, joined the Laurent-Perrier group at the end of the 1980s, though each has its own wines.

traps: Grand Siècle is multi vintage by design, not an undeclared vintage wine.
Grand Siècle has no e: siècle is masculine. La Grande Année is Bollinger's, La Grande Dame is Veuve Clicquot's and Grande Cuvée is Krug's.
Laurent-Perrier rosé is macerated, not blended, even though blending is legal here.
Laurent-Perrier is not Perrier-Jouët: one house is of Tours-sur-Marne with Grand Siècle, the other of Épernay with Belle Époque.

sheet.label: Grand Siècle, with its Itération number
sheet.note: The sheet and the label agree, Grand Siècle with no e because siècle is masculine; since 2019 the label also prints the Itération, such as Itération 26.

questions.q: Which prestige cuvée is blended on purpose from three vintages and released as a numbered Itération?
questions.exp: Grand Siècle is Laurent-Perrier's three vintage blend. La Grande Année is Bollinger's vintage wine, La Grande Dame is Veuve Clicquot's and Belle Époque is Perrier-Jouët's, each of a single vintage.

questions.q: Which wine did Laurent-Perrier first release in 1968?
opts: The Cuvée Rosé, made by maceration
questions.exp: The Cuvée Rosé, Pinot Noir macerated on its skins, came in 1968. Ultra Brut followed in 1981, and Les Réserves is a late disgorged Grand Siècle in magnum.

questions.q: From which villages does the fruit of Grand Siècle Itération 26 come?

report: Built on the library's p-laurent-perrier and its traps, contradicting none of it; the house has no flagships record. The region record's producers line calls the rosé a saignée, where the library and the house say maceration: the owner may want the region line read, and nothing here edits it.

The founder, the cellar master and his widow are described and not named: their dates were not found in two sources, and the founder's first name differs between accounts (André Michel or Alphonse Pierlot). The widow's name lives in the label Laurent-Perrier.

The woman who bought the house in 1939, born into the Lanson family and the mother of Bernard de Nonancourt, is described and not named, because her dates were not found; the sale is dated 1939 by Wikipedia and Vinepair, 1938 by one UPI obituary.
Bernard de Nonancourt (1920 to 2010) is dated by Wikipedia and World of Fine Wine; head of the house from 1948 by the house's own history.

Grand Siècle's first release: 1959 with the 1952, 1953 and 1955 vintages by The Finest Bubble, The Buyer and an Idealwine obituary; 1960 by Decanter's obituary and Wikipedia; the record gives 1959 and says both.

The Itération number on the bottle from 2019, Itérations 24 and 22 in magnum, is The Finest Bubble's and Falstaff's; Itération 25's vintages are Falstaff's and The Drinks Business's; Itération 26's vintages, crus, ten years and blend are the house's.

The sites and the blend of Itération 26 follow the house's magazine page: eight Grands Crus and 58 per cent Chardonnay; the house's product page gives 52 and 48 and adds Chouilly, Mailly and Verzenay, which a reader of a back label should weigh.
Dosage: 7 grams a litre for Itérations 23 and 25 by the house's magazine and for Itération 26 by a merchant.

Left out: the stainless steel tanks of the 1950s or the 1970s (merchants disagree), the shape of the bottle (no source found), La Cuvée's shares and reserve figures (merchants disagree), and malolactic, which no page read states, so style.malolactic is empty.
kind.code: the letters NM were not read on a label; the inference rests on the house buying grapes beyond its own vines, and a refuter should read a label.
The young glass is Falstaff's and Gault and Millau's on Itération 26; no note of an older bottle was sourced, and the aged field says so rather than invent one.

Les Réserves, Itération 20: 21 years under cork in magnum and the second after Itération 17 are Decanter's, with World of Fine Wine's more than twenty years; the record writes Itération 26 where the label sets a number sign before the figure.

changed: story: The cause of the decline had no source; the daughter's years are in two accounts; the buyer of 1939 is dead and her dates were not found, so the brief asks that she be described.
cuvee.making: Itération 26's shares stand on Decanter and the house's magazine; Itération 25's were not confirmed.
table.house45: The Grand Vin Sans Sucre was the widow's, at the end of the nineteenth century; Ultra Brut of 1981 is its rebirth.
